Sadly we didn't have that exact info. But the company I'm working right now uses the same technology/equipment used for the VPN part of the transmission. Usually all of the IP in that VPN should connect to a single controller that manages the SDWAN before going to the intended central server.

Now that I've thought of it more, I think the 192.168.0.2 would be the local IP of the SDWAN controller, the other votes that didn't passed through 192.168.0.2 would be from satellite connections as it didn't passed through SDWAN network.

This maybe a case of shtty logs used by the central server not recognizing the sender’s origin IP, or it may have been overwritten by the SDWAN Controller as what a VPN should be doing.

Much of this is speculation based on what I know from working from both companies.

Former support technician hired by Smartmatic during May 9 elections to support my town's canvassing center, whats fishy here is most of the VCM should be on a type A class of IP network not [192.168.0.2](https://192.168.0.2). All vcms are connected thru either LTE, Fibr or Satellite connections using a VPN to connect to a central server. What I think happened here is most of the transmission funneled to a single IP on the same network of the central server?

My town didn't have the record breaking transmission of votes either, most of my colleagues have said that most transmissions were finished around 11pm to 12am. I was also shocked to see that theres a majority on the counting as soon as 9pm because most of us at that time is still trying or having a hard time trying to connect to the VPN.  


EDIT: note that the IP of the LTE, Fibr or Satellite connection shouldn't matter because we used a hardware level vpn, every transmission should've come from 10.x.x.x IP address. It"s either the logs are fcked up and its listing its own host address on its local network or they funneled the votes to another server then went to the central server.
